chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Ashyam, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
'Do you know why Ishmael was called the Truthful of the Promise?' He said, 'I do not know.' So he said, 'He made a promise to a man and sat for him for a year waiting for him.'

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ: Ishmael, a Prophet of God, son of Abraham
key_terms.حَوْلًا: A year, a period of time
key_terms.صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ: Truthful of the Promise, a title denoting fidelity to one's word

ai.seo_question: Why is the Prophet Ishmael referred to as 'Sadiq al-Wa'd' (Truthful of the Promise)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the epithet 'Sadiq al-Wa'd' for Prophet Ishmael by highlighting his exemplary adherence to promises, specifically illustrating his patient vigil for a full year awaiting a promised meeting. This narrative, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the Shia emphasis on *siddqiyyah* (truthfulness) as a defining trait of the prophets, linking Ishmael’s personal integrity to the broader theological concept of divine fidelity.
